Hyderabad - 500 058 |telephone = |campus = |website = |footnotes = |country=[[India]]}} '''Defence Metallurgical Research Laboratory''' ('''DMRL''') is a [[research laboratory]] of the [[Defence Research and Development Organisation]] (DRDO). Located in Defence Research Complex, [[Kanchanbagh]], [[Hyderabad, Andhra Pradesh|Hyderabad]]. It is responsible for the development and manufacture of complex metals and materials required for modern warfare and weapon systems.{{cite book |doi=10.1007/978-981-99-5060-7_15 |chapter=Defence Metallurgical Research Laboratory: Relentless Journey Towards Materials Galore |title=Indian Metallurgy |series=Indian Institute of Metals Series |date=2024 |last1=Madhusudhan Reddy |first1=G. |pages=179–200 |isbn=978-981-99-5059-1 }}{{Cite web |date=28 March 2017 |title=DRDO Laboratories and their Research Activities |url=https://pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=160059 |access-date=2023-12-28 |website=Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Defence, Government of India.}} ==History== As with all the labs of DRDO, Defence Metallurgical Research Laboratory (DMRL) was an extension out of the Technical Development Establishment (Metals) which was earlier called the Inspectorate of Metals and Steel situated at Ishapore (near Kolkata).{{cite web |title=Welcome to Metal & Steel Factory, Ishapore |url=https://ddpdoo.gov.in/units/MSF |website=Metal & Steel Factory, Ishapore |publisher=Government of India |access-date=28 December 2023}}{{cite web |title=Metal and Steel Factory, Ishapore |url=https://www.defstrat.com/magazine_articles/metal-and-steel-factory-ishapore/ |website=Defstrat |publisher=South Asia Defence & Strategic Review |access-date=28 December 2023}} DMRL was shifted to Hyderabad in 1963. Since then, it has developed competence in the areas of powder metallurgy based fabrication and development of alloys, armor and rocket motor steel, aerospace light alloys, and magnetic materials. The formation of other entities such as the [[Mishra Dhatu Nigam]] Ltd., [[High Energy Projectile Factory]] (formerly Heavy Alloy Penetrator Project), Composites Production Centre, Non-Ferrous Technology Development Centre, and the Advanced Research Centre International have followed the establishment of DMRL.{{Cite news |date=2025-09-04 |title=DMRL transfers three advanced materials tech to industry |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/dmrl-transfers-three-advanced-materials-tech-to-industry/article70011547.ece |access-date=2025-09-30 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}} The DMRL is also involved in [[R&D]] efforts to develop futuristic materials to provide advanced technology options.{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2023-11-27 |title=New facility opened in Midhani on its 50th anniversary |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/new-facility-opened-in-midhani-on-its-50th-anniversary/article67580321.ece |access-date=2023-12-28 |issn=0971-751X}} ==Projects and products== * DMR 1700 ultra-high-strength steel with the toughness stronger than 250 [[maraging steel]] but cost is 60% lower; this steel has been used to build rocket motor casings for the [[Akash surface-to-air missile]]s.{{Cite web |title=Defence Metallurgical Research Laboratory |url=https://www.nti.org/education-center/facilities/defence-metallurgical-research-laboratory/ |access-date=28 December 2023 |website=Nuclear Threat Initiative}}{{cite journal |last1=Gurrappa |first1=I. |last2=Malakondaiah |first2=G. |title=Corrosion characteristics of DMR-1700 steel and comparison with different steels in marine environment |journal=Materials Science and Engineering: A |date=January 2005 |volume=391 |issue=1–2 |pages=235–242 |doi=10.1016/j.msea.2004.08.079 }}{{cite journal |last1=Gurrappa |first1=I. |last2=Malakondaiah |first2=G. |title=Corrosion characteristics of newly developed structural DMR-1700 steel and comparison with different steels for industrial applications |journal=Metallurgical and Materials Transactions A |date=October 2006 |volume=37 |issue=10 |pages=3039–3046 |doi=10.1007/s11661-006-0185-9 |bibcode=2006MMTA...37.3039G }} * DMR SN 742 is a nickel based superalloy used in turbine rotors and compressor and optimized for manufacturing, also cheaper compared to other alternatives.{{cite web | url=https://www.iadb.in/2022/02/23/development-of-nickel-base-superalloy-components-for-aeroengine-applications/ | title=Development of Nickel-Base Superalloy & Components for Aeroengine Applications | Indian Aerospace and Defence Bulletin - News for aerospace and defence in India | date=23 February 2022 }}{{cite journal |last1=Sahithya |first1=K. |last2=Balasundar |first2=I. |last3=Pant |first3=Prita |last4=Raghu |first4=T. |title=Primary hot working characteristics of an as-cast and homogenized nickel base superalloy DMR-742 in the sub and super-solvus temperature regime |journal=Journal of Alloys and Compounds |date=April 2020 |volume=821 |article-number=153455 |doi=10.1016/j.jallcom.2019.153455 }} * DMR 249A is a low carbon micro-alloyed grade of steel with stringent toughness requirement at sub-zero temperature.grade was having the specified gas contents of hydrogen <2 ppm in final product for the avoidance of detrimental phenomenon like “Hair Line Cracks”. So the Hydrogen content of liquid steel was to be less than 3 ppm and this demand vacuum treatment of the steel.{{Cite news |last=Mazumdar |first=Rakhi |date=2017-10-16 |title=SAIL supplied defence grade steel plates for anti-submarine warship INS Kiltan |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/indl-goods/svs/steel/sail-supplied-defence-grade-steel-plates-for-anti-submarine-warship-ins-kiltan/articleshow/61103851.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2023-08-01 |issn=0013-0389}} * GTM-900 titanium alloy, DMRL collaborated with [[National Aerospace Laboratories|NAL]] to develop this alpha-beta titanium alloy for aerospace applications, This alloy has been engineered to provide high strength, creep resistance, and stability under high temperatures.{{cite journal |last1=Thammaiah |first1=B. R. |last2=Fernando |first2=Chandru D. |last3=Majila |first3=Anuradha Nayak |last4=Anilchandra |first4=A. R. |last5=Nandana |first5=M. S. |last6=Bhat |first6=Udaya K. |last7=Manjunatha |first7=C. M. |title=High Strain Rate Behavior of GTM-900 Titanium Alloy |journal=Materials Performance and Characterization |date=24 June 2021 |volume=10 |issue=2 |pages=195–206 |doi=10.1520/MPC20200157 }}{{cite web | url=https://www.nal.res.in/en/publication/high-strain-rate-behavior-gtm-900-titanium-alloy | title=High strain rate behavior of GTM-900 titanium alloy - CSIR - NAL }} * TITAN 26A and TITAN 29A are high-temperature titanium alloys developed by DMRL and [[Mishra Dhatu Nigam|MIDHANI]], they are used for manufacturing critical components like compressor discs, blades, and shafts for engines, including those for Adour (Jaguar aircraft) and [[GTRE GTX-35VS Kaveri|Kaveri]] aircraft engines.{{cite web | url=https://www.drdo.gov.in/drdo/high-temperature-titanium-alloys-components | title=High Temperature Titanium Alloys & Components | Defence Research and Development Organisation - DRDO, Ministry of Defence, Government of India }} * Ultra light Mg-Li alloy, In the mid-1980s, a research programme was initiated at DMRL, Mg-Li-AI alloys were made by mixing molten magnesium and aluminium-magnesium master alloy in a mild steel crucible at around 1023 K and pouring over molten lithium, separately melted in a stainless steel crucible and kept at around 573 K. The melt was then chill-cast in a mild steel mould. Interest was shown by Lockheed Company, USA for obtaining magnesium-lithium alloy sheets from DMRL. Wrought products (plates/sheets) of magnesium-lithium alloy have been supplied to ISAC, Bangalore and are being used in their [[INSAT-2E|INSAT-2]] programme.{{cite journal |last1=Chakravorty |first1=C R |title=Development of ultra light magnesium-lithium alloys |journal=Bulletin of Materials Science |date=November 1994 |volume=17 |issue=6 |pages=733–745 |doi=10.1007/BF02757554 }} * Jackal steel is an advanced grade high strength low alloy steel, The technology of Jackal steel has been passed on to [[Steel Authority of India Limited]] (SAIL) and [[Mishra Dhatu Nigam]] (MIDHANI) for its bulk production.{{Cite news |date=3 August 2016 |title=Rourkela Steel Plant supplies parts for Agni Missile |work=Business Standard |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/rourkela-steel-plant-supplies-parts-for-agni-missile-116080301419_1.html |access-date=28 December 2023}} * DMRL has developed technologies for large scale production of titanium, magnesium metals and Mg-Ti alloys.https://www.ias.ac.in/article/fulltext/boms/019/06/0921-0938 * DMRL has developed indigenous titanium sponge making process and transferred technology to [[Kerala Minerals and Metals|KMML]] in [[Titanium Sponge Plant]].{{cite web | url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/in-other-news/221116/kerala-minerals-and-metals-ltd-begins-titanium-sponge-sale.html | title=Kerala Minerals and Metals Ltd begins titanium sponge sale | date=22 November 2016 }} * Heavy alloy pre-fragments for [[Prithvi missile]] warheads developed for use against aerial targets. * [[Oxygen-free copper]] for the [[Nag anti-tank guided missile]] sheets.{{cite web |last1=Singh |first1=Manjit |title=Ammunition Systems and Warhead Technologies |url=https://www.drdo.gov.in/sites/default/files/technology-focus-documrnt/TF_Feb_2017_WEB.pdf |publisher=Defence Research & Development Organisation |access-date=28 December 2023}} * Special magnetic materials such as [[samarium-cobalt ring magnet]]s and [[neodymium-iron-boron magnet]]s in collaboration with the [[Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre]] for applications in the space program. * [[Kanchan armour]] for use on the [[Arjun (tank)|Arjun]] tank as well as other armoured vehicles like Sarath and Abhay. * Under [[DRDO]]-[[FICCI]] Accelerated Technology Assessment & Commercialization initiative, DMRL supplied its patented Copper-Titanium (CuTi) alloy technology for commercial application to Pahwa Metal Tech and has also granted an exclusive license to manufacture products using the technology and sell them aboard.{{Cite news |date=7 July 2016 |title=Copper-Titanium alloy to be made first time in India by a Pune startup |work=Business Standard |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/news-cm/copper-titanium-alloy-to-be-made-first-time-in-india-by-a-pune-startup-116070700692_1.html |access-date=28 December 2023}} * High Nitrogen Steel (HNS), created by DMRL and [[Jindal Stainless Limited]], will be used in armaments that will replace [[Rolled homogeneous armour|Rolled Homogenous Armour]] (RHA). It is corrosion resistant with reduced thickness that increases fuel and mass efficiency, has superior ballistic and blast protection, plus higher longevity. HNS has higher impact value, higher energy absorption level, which improves overall crash worthiness. It has passed multiple levels of ballistic tests in different calibers with 8-10 times higher impact protection.{{Cite web |last=Sundarajan |first=Priya |date=2017-03-01 |title=Jindal Stainless enters defence arena, teams up with DRDO |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/jindal-stainless-enters-defence-arena-teams-up-with-drdo/article9565177.ece |access-date=2023-12-28 |website=BusinessLine |language=en}} *Developed high strength metastable [[Beta-titanium]] alloy, Ti-10V-2Fe-3Al on industrial scale for applications in aerospace structural forgings.{{Cite news|date=2021-07-20|title=DRDO develops high strength titanium alloy for aerospace forgings|language=en-IN|work=The Hindu|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/drdo-develops-high-strength-titanium-alloy-for-aerospace-forgings/article35421043.ece|access-date=2021-07-20|issn=0971-751X}} Will replace traditional Ni-Cr-Mo structural steels to achieve weight reduction. The landing gear drop link is the first component forged successfully by the [[Aeronautical Development Agency]] (ADA) at [[Hindustan Aeronautics Limited]] (HAL) and has been certified for airworthiness.{{Cite news |last=Rao |first=Ch Sushil |date=2021-07-20 |title=DRDO indigenously develops high strength beta titanium alloy on industrial scale |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/drdo-indigenously-develops-high-strength-beta-titanium-alloy-on-industrial-scale/articleshow/84579811.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2023-12-28 |issn=0971-8257}} *Successfully developed near isothermal forging technology for aero engines in 2021. It can help produce all the five stages of high-pressure compressors (HPC) discs out of difficult-to-deform titanium alloy using 2000 MT isothermal forge press weighing 2,000 tonnes. The technology has been transferred to MIDHANI for bulk production. DMRL has also supplied 200 HPC disc forgings for various compressor stages to HAL for fitment in [[Rolls-Royce Turbomeca Adour]] that powers the [[SEPECAT Jaguar]] and [[BAE Systems Hawk]] of Indian Air Force.{{Cite news |date=28 May 2021 |title=DRDO develops near isothermal forging technology for aeroengines' parts |work=Business Standard |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/drdo-develops-near-isothermal-forging-technology-for-aeroengines-parts-121052801543_1.html |access-date=28 December 2023}}{{cite news |title=DRDO develops Critical Near Isothermal Forging Technology for aeroengines |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1722418 |access-date=28 December 2023 |agency=Press Information Bureau |publisher=Ministry of Defence |date=28 May 2021}} *In 2021, DMRL achieved the breakthrough in design and development of [[Single crystal|single-crystal]] casting technology for [[turbine blade]]s. They supplied 60 high pressure turbine (HPT) blades of nickel-based super alloy to HAL for helicopter engine applications under indigenous helicopter development programme.{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2021-04-26 |title=DRDO develops critical crystal blade technology for aero engines |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/drdo-develops-critical-crystal-blade-technology-for-aero-engines/article34415540.ece |access-date=2023-12-28 |issn=0971-751X}} * Tungsten plated silica/graphite aerogel, DMRL along with BARC is developing tungsten casting technology on silica/graphite aerogel for ultra high temperature aerospace engine applications.{{Cite web |date=January 2007 |title=Casting and Characterization of Aerogel Objects in Metallic Moulds |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/S-Ingale/publication/258022748_Casting_and_Characterization_of_Aerogel_Objects_in_Metallic_Moulds/links/00b49526a078e6037b000000/Casting-and-Characterization-of-Aerogel-Objects-in-Metallic-Moulds.pdf |access-date=19 Oct 2025 |website=researchgate.net}} ==Collaboration== DRDO (DMRL) has transferred technologies of its DMR 249A Steel Sheets & Plates for naval applications and DMR 1700 mill forms for extract: Defence Metallurgical Research Laboratory (DMRL) is a research laboratory of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO).
